meta.title: Ezequiel Fernández | Open Source Contributions | Full Stack Developer
meta.description: Three merged pull requests in open source repositories: two fixes in vitest and one in @fastify/cookie. Every PR is public and verifiable on GitHub.

title: Open source contributions
intro: Three pull requests merged into projects I do not own. I am not a maintainer and not a regular contributor: I am a contributor. Each entry below has the problem, the fix and the review, with a link to the public PR if you want to read the diff.

vitestVmDeps.problem: The vm pools ran Vite's dependency optimizer over the whole index.html. If a dependency discovered that way could not be bundled, the run died with exit 1 while every test passed. That is the worst kind of failure: it does not say a test is wrong, it says the process crashed.
vitestVmDeps.change: The configEnvironment handler returned early for the vm environment before applying resolveOptimizerConfig, so that environment kept Vite's browser default. I traced it back to the commit that introduced it and the fix was merged. The maintainer added wording nits and clarified the fixture before approving.
vitestVmDeps.review: RED → GREEN: without the fix exactly vmThreads and vmForks fail; with the fix all four pools pass.

fastifyCookieEncode.problem: reply.setCookie() accepted an encode option and ignored it: it never forwarded it to the cookie@2 serializer, so there was no way to customise how the value is encoded. A silent failure: the option goes in, nothing happens.
fastifyCookieEncode.change: I separated encode from the rest of the attributes and passed it as stringifySetCookie options. It was merged with two maintainer approvals and shipped in @fastify/cookie 11.1.5, minutes after the merge.
fastifyCookieEncode.review: An earlier PR had the same goal. Instead of closing mine, I explained how it differed; the maintainers merged both and the code that survived is mine. The PR took 32.6 days to land.

vitestCacheUnwritable.problem: Since 5.0.4 the on-disk module cache is enabled by default. If its directory could not be created —a read-only filesystem, or a project owned by another user— the mkdirSync threw, and the module being transformed failed with an error that had nothing to do with the test.
vitestCacheUnwritable.change: I measured that the failure hit the first module of each config, not every file as the report claimed. Instead of propagating the error, the cache degrades: it reports the directory as unusable once and returns the same null value that already meant "this module is not cached".
vitestCacheUnwritable.review: The maintainer requested changes: he wanted the whole feature disabled so no hashes were computed for nothing. My first version caught the error where the mkdir lived, which is too late. I moved the check to the start of the traversal: it does not read, does not hash, does not write. The final design is smaller than mine and better.

verification.heading: Why you can verify this
verification.paragraph: Every card links the public pull request on GitHub: the diff, who approved it, who merged it, and what was discussed in review are all there. I do not list open or rejected PRs, because an open PR is an intention and can still close without being merged.
